clue.text: Shamefaced husband admitted to date with Penny, a single mum

indicators.note: something admitted to a place is let inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to see someone is to date them
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit
mum as in keep mum: SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A man caught going out with a single mother called Penny looks embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not a mother at all: it means silent, as in keeping mum, giving SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone embarrassed and abashed, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Grasping women finish first and cheat

indicators.note: the finishing letter moves to the front of the word

parts.note: harpies are greedy, rapacious women

explanation.surface: Greedy women win the race and cheat to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish first' sounds like winning; it moves the last S to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A card sharp or swindler is a slang name for a cheat.

clue.text: A certain vice president backed by America's providing gratification

indicators.note: backed means the letters are written backwards

parts.note: one means a certain person, as in one Mr Smith
Al Gore was US vice president

explanation.surface: A particular deputy leader is supported by America's patronage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses ONE GORE, giving EROGENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing parts of the body that give sexual pleasure when touched.

clue.text: One's paid pop star for nothing

parts.note: a professional is one who is paid
Bono is the lead singer of U2

explanation.surface: A paid professional hires a famous singer to work for free.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase used of professional work, especially legal, done free of charge.

clue.text: Holy Grail ultimately isn't a hit? That's unknown

indicators.note: hit as in struck and knocked about, so the letters are scrambled
ultimately means take the last letter

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the Holy Grail is a hit, and admits nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like success, but it rearranges ISNTA into SAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Godly and virtuous, as a saint is, is a synonym for holy.

clue.text: Careless sister, heading off, runs into street

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a sister in a religious order is a nun

indicators.note: runs goes into street, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a way is a road or street
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A careless nun, eyes elsewhere, dashes out into the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sister' looks like family but is a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone careless is not on guard, the sense of being off one's guard.

clue.text: Sell short skirts from unknown period (including slip)

indicators.note: skirts are the edges, so take the outer letters
including means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a date is a period of time
to err is to slip up

explanation.surface: Cheap skirts from an unknown era, with a petticoat thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' and 'slip' look like clothing; they mean edges and a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone short is to fail to value them properly, the idiom matching this verb.

clue.text: Nick's in decline, but hopeful

indicators.note: Nick is in decline, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to wane is to decline
to nick is to nab, to catch

explanation.surface: Nick's career is fading but he remains optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is the verb to arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for an aspiring person who wants to be famous, a hopeful.

clue.text: Let in again to study with Cambridge University

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A student is re-admitted to study at Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge University' is not the English one but MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow back in or re-admit, the verb formed with the prefix for again.

clue.text: A game plan almost goes west, having admitted fault

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, backwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a design is a plan

explanation.surface: A team's tactics fall apart and someone owns up to the mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DESIGN to DESIG, which 'goes west' turns to GISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To say sorry is to concede that one was in the wrong, so the past tense matches the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Close tavern early, kicking some characters out

indicators.note: throwing out the surrounding letters leaves a run of letters concealed inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A landlord shuts the pub ahead of time and throws out some of the regulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb about shutting the pub; it is the adjective meaning nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Close in the sense of nearby or not far away is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Could be Lord Alfred Tennyson's first poem, without date, lost around here

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the word here, holding it inside
lost suggests the letters have gone astray and are rearranged
without means the following letter is removed
first means take only the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tribute to a Victorian poet laureate, losing a date and a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson really was a lord, so the surface is apt. 'without' drops D from Alfred; 'lost' scrambles the letters, which go 'around' the word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is one example of a hereditary noble with a seat in the upper house, hence 'Could be'.

clue.text: Organisation of money of country, principally?

definitions.text: Organisation of money of country, principally?

indicators.note: organisation means the letters are arranged in a new order
principally means taking the leading letters of the words

explanation.surface: A question about how a nation's finances are arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: MONEY plus O and C from 'of country' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's financial system, how its wealth is managed, is described by this word.

clue.text: April here, meaning this military review?

definitions.meaning: when April is here, the previous month has gone by
a parade of troops filing past a saluting officer

explanation.surface: Spring arrives, and with it a parade of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: by April, the month before has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial parade in which troops pass an inspecting dignitary is a kind of review.

clue.text: Lord accepts a joke, displaying dignity

indicators.note: something that accepts another takes it in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: My! is an exclamation like Lord!
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A nobleman takes a joke in good part and shows his composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' is not a peer here: it is the exclamation, like 'My!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty means stately grandeur, a synonym for dignity.

clue.text: Do nasty kids hold artist up? That's right

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
to hold is to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
brats are badly behaved children

explanation.surface: Do horrible children hold up a painter? Yes, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DRAOBRATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel.

clue.text: Daughter's rodent problem returned — pungent stuff required

indicators.note: returned means the letters come back the other way

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A girl's pest problem has come back, so something strong is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' sounds like trouble but is a school sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The condiment made from seeds has a hot, sharp flavour, fairly called pungent.

clue.text: This country abuts Russia's borders in east

definitions.text: This country abuts Russia's borders in east

parts.note: for a British setter, this country is the UK

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so take the outer letters

explanation.surface: A geography fact: a nation shares its eastern border with Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the nation's eastern frontier is Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The European nation whose eastern frontier runs along Russia matches the whole description.

clue.text: Fungus is to irritate after short time

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ruffle someone is to irritate them

explanation.surface: A mushroom annoys someone after only a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A prized edible underground fungus is called this.

clue.text: Literary giant's novel is read outside Portugal

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the other piece, enclosing it
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A great writer's book is being read in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal; the giant is a character, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant Despair is the ogre of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress.

clue.text: Duke conceals first name in prison, creating indignation

indicators.note: conceals means one letter covers another, replacing it
first says it is the earlier of the prison word's two name letters that is covered

parts.note: a dungeon is an underground prison

explanation.surface: A nobleman hides his identity while locked up, causing resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' means D covers the first N of DUNGEON, replacing it.
explanation.definitionFit: In high dudgeon means deeply offended, so the word means resentment or anger.

clue.text: Back in embrace of woman, still you soundly sleep

indicators.note: held in a woman's embrace means placed inside her

parts.note: she refers to a woman

indicators.note: soundly signals a word heard rather than written

parts.note: the word you, spoken, is just the letter U

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round

parts.note: yet means still, as in not yet

explanation.surface: Back in a woman's arms, you can still sleep soundly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses YET to TEY; 'soundly' gives U for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a nap or a stretch of sleep.

clue.text: Beast's command to beloved oarsman overheard?

indicators.note: overheard means the phrase is caught by ear, so it is judged by sound

parts.note: telling a loved rower to get going: row, dear

explanation.surface: An animal's voice is caught urging on a sweetheart in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small deer is an animal, so the general word beast covers it.

clue.text: Cryptic hint for nut blamed for scuffle?

parts.note: rough as an anagram signal applied to the letters of AND TUMBLE would produce these two words

explanation.surface: A crazy person gets the blame for a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: ROUGH is an anagram signal working on AND TUMBLE, which gives 'nut blamed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy, disorderly fight or tussle is described by this phrase, a synonym for scuffle.

clue.text: Willingly romance female

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful tales, to lie

explanation.surface: A woman happily embarks on a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' is a verb meaning to tell fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb, as in I'd as lief go, meaning gladly.

clue.text: Declare top grade in history, having worried about studies on vacation

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: ever means at any time, anywhere in history
to eat at someone is to worry them, so ate means worried

explanation.surface: Someone states they got the best mark in history after fretting over studies in the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'history' looks like a school subject; 'in history' means EVER, at any time.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal verb meaning to state solemnly or affirm, a synonym for declare.

clue.text: Feel bitter about heartless doctor in hospital

indicators.note: heartless means the central letters are removed

parts.note: a resident is a doctor living in at a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone harbours a grudge about an unfeeling medic on the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' seems to describe the doctor's manner but strips ID from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To take offence at something and hold a grudge is a direct synonym.

clue.text: First off, humans must have sex to breed

indicators.note: first off means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: men are humans in the general sense
gender is a person's sex

explanation.surface: People must have sex in order to reproduce, first and foremost.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is to bring about or produce, the same as to cause or generate.
